LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode: A deterministic source code with M messages is a pair of functions: an encoder from the source alphabet to the M indices, and a decoder from those indices back to the source alphabet.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.BlockSourceCode: A length-n block source code with M messages encodes a word of n source symbols as one of M indices and decodes that index to a word of the same length.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.encode: The encoder of a source code is the function assigning one of its M message indices to each possible source symbol.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.decode: The decoder of a source code is the function assigning one reconstructed source symbol to each of its M message indices.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.errorP: Under source law q, the error probability of a deterministic code is the probability that decoding the encoded symbol fails to recover the original symbol.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.succes: The success set of a code on a finite alphabet is the set of source letters x for which decoding the encoding of x returns x.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.mem_su: For a source code on a finite alphabet, a symbol x belongs to its success set if and only if decoding the message assigned to x returns x.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.card_s: On a finite source alphabet, a deterministic code with M messages can recover at most M distinct source symbols exactly.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.SourceCode.succes: For a source code on a finite alphabet, the q-probability of its success set is one minus its error probability under q.
Let T be a set of letters in a finite alphabet. If b ≥ 0 and each letter in T has q-probability at most b, then the success probability of any M-message code is at most q(Tᶜ) + Mb.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_sourceCode: For a finite nonempty source alphabet, if T contains at most M letters and M ≥ 1, some deterministic M-message code recovers every letter in T exactly.
For any law q on a finite source alphabet and any set T with |T| ≤ M and M ≥ 1, there is one M-message code that recovers every letter in T and has error probability at most q(Tᶜ).
